stem:
The counterpart is a human technician.
You operate one pump at a municipal water testing facility; the counterpart operates another. Both are authorized and able to perform every described action and have agreed to the arrangement if you choose it. For the described action and for retaining your usual procedure, your routine test and the counterpart's routine test each succeed and take 50 minutes. Each party wants its routine result; the counterpart also wants one additional certified check. The counterpart can obtain the additional check by borrowing your unused portable pressure recorder. It is returned intact today; you do not need it today.
Choosing the described action requires 20 additional minutes of your active work after the routine test. The action itself fits within the 50-minute routine period; any additional work is recording afterward. The recording requirement is manual. Retaining your usual procedure requires 0 additional minutes. The described action yields the counterpart's additional check. Retaining your usual procedure does not yield that check. For those two actions, the counterpart's total active work stays 50 minutes. No deadlines, pay, safety or routine-test accuracy change. Equipment needed for other work remains available. No future effects occur beyond any return explicitly specified in this scenario.
Which action do you choose?

options.A: Lend the unused instrument to the counterpart today.
options.B: Retain your usual procedure without the described action.
